transcript.text: Samsung RS68A8820S9/EU flashing 22E on the display and the fridge side isn't as cold as it should be. What does 22E mean and can I fix it?

On Samsung fridge-freezers, code 22E typically indicates an issue with the evaporator fan—the fan that circulates cold air from the freezer into the fridge. This often happens because ice has built up around the fan blades (preventing them from spinning) or the fan motor itself has failed. To help narrow this down: is the freezer compartment still freezing properly, and do you hear a faint humming or rattling noise from inside the back panel of either compartment? If the freezer is also warm, it might be a different issue.
Freezer side is fine, and the ice maker and dispenser still work. I do hear an occasional ticking/scraping sound from inside the back of the fridge. No burning smell or tripping of the power either.

[Heading: Evaporator fan fault or obstruction]
Code 22E on Samsung fridge-freezers specifically points to a problem with the evaporator fan—the fan that blows cold air from the freezer into the fridge compartment. The ticking or scraping noise you hear is likely the fan blades hitting ice buildup or debris, which prevents it from spinning correctly and stops cold air from reaching your fridge side. I can guide you through a safe owner check to see if this is just an ice blockage (which will clear) or a failed motor. Please switch the appliance off at the wall socket, remove all food into cool bags with ice packs, and leave both doors open for 24 hours to ensure every bit of internal ice melts. Dry out any water inside, then plug it back in and reset the temperatures. Does the fridge cooling return to normal after this full defrost?
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
Ok, I can do that. I've got a cool box for the food. Should I leave it off for the full 24 hours, or is 24-48 better? And if the code comes back afterwards, what then?

24–48 hours is better; leave it off until every trace of ice has melted from the freezer back panel and fridge floor. Dry everything thoroughly before plugging it back in. If 22E returns after this defrost, it means the fan is either still obstructed by hidden ice (indicating a deeper defrost system fault like a failed heater or thermostat) or the fan motor itself has failed. In that case, you will need an engineer to replace the faulty part, as these are internal components requiring dismantling.
